title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Intégration de [dg-]algèbres simpliciales', i.e. integration on simplicial differential graded groups.

**Setup.** Let A be a simplicial object in differential graded abelian groups, with d of degree +1. Write A_n = ⊕_p A_n^p. Hypothesis (1) has two parts:
- A_n^p = 0 for p outside [0,n].
- The augmentation ε_n : A_0 → A_n^* is a resolution of A_0. Here A_0 is in degree 0 with zero differential, and ε_n is induced by the unique map Δ_n → Δ_0. This is an abstract Poincaré lemma on each simplex.

The face maps give ∂ = Σ_i (−1)^i ∂_{n,i}^* : A_n^i → A_{n−1}^i, with ∂∂ = 0. Implicitly ∂ commutes with d, since the faces are DG maps.

**Proposition 1.** There is a unique family of group homomorphisms K_n : A_n → A_0 such that:
- (a) K_0 = id.
- (b) K_n vanishes on A_n^p for p ≠ n.
- (c) Stokes: K_n(dω) = K_{n−1}(∂ω).

By (b), condition (c) has content only for ω ∈ A_n^{n−1}.

**Proof (induction on N).** Take ϖ ∈ A_N^N. It is closed because A_N^{N+1} = 0, hence exact by (1), say ϖ = dη. Put K_N(ϖ) = K_{N−1}(∂η). Grothendieck remarks that only H^N(A_N) = 0 for N ≥ 1 is needed. Uniqueness is clear.

**Margin note.** The system K is natural with respect to morphisms of simplicial DG groups.

**What it serves.** This is the abstract axiomatic version of fibre integration ∫_{Δ^n} for polynomial or divided-power differential forms on standard simplices. It is the ingredient for the de Rham comparison map A(X) → C^*(X; A_0), sending ω to (σ ↦ K_n(σ^*ω)). By Stokes this map is a chain map.

The context is the divided-power de Rham complex over Z (1976 IHÉS lecture). There, divided powers make the Poincaré lemma hold integrally, so the hypotheses are satisfied. The page is sandwiched between a misfiled page of Sullivan-style minimal-model notes in English and a page from SGA 7 IX.
errors: Well-definedness of K_N is not written out. If dη = dη', then η − η' is closed. For N ≥ 2 it is exact, η − η' = dζ, and K_{N−1}(∂dζ) = K_{N−1}(d∂ζ) = K_{N−2}(∂∂ζ) = 0. For N = 1, η − η' = ε(a) and ∂ε(a) = a − a = 0. So the argument works, but it uses the unstated compatibility d∂ = ∂d and the lower-degree acyclicity.
The page does not check that the K_n defined this way satisfy Stokes in all degrees. It does hold trivially by (b) when the degree is not n−1.
The text is a fragment: the derived comparison map to simplicial cochains is not written on this page.

ideas.what: Axiomatic characterization: integration over simplices is uniquely determined by normalization, degree and Stokes, for any simplicial DG group satisfying a Poincaré lemma with forms concentrated in degrees [0,n].
ideas.modern_name: Integration map / de Rham comparison for simplicial cdga's of forms (Sullivan ∇(p,*), Bousfield–Gugenheim ∮); uniqueness via acyclicity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977), Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976) for rational forms; integral divided-power versions by Cenkl–Porter (early 1980s) and later Karoubi
ideas.where_published: unpublished; 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex, apparently not written up

ideas.what: Naturality of the integration system with respect to morphisms of simplicial DG groups (margin note).

missed.claim: This is a clean abstract formulation: any simplicial DG group that is acyclic over A_0 in each simplicial degree and has forms in degrees [0,n] carries a unique Stokes-compatible integration. It applies directly to divided-power polynomial forms over Z. The idea is elementary, but it documents Grothendieck's own 1976 approach to an integral de Rham theorem with divided powers, which predates or parallels Cenkl–Porter's integral forms.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it credits Grothendieck with the divided-power integral de Rham / integral cochain-model approach (relevant to integral and p-adic homotopy-theory models). It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine acyclic-models style uniqueness argument. The interest is historical: Grothendieck worked on integral divided-power simplicial de Rham theory in 1976, a topic usually credited to Cenkl–Porter and others.

The line after (c) likely reads 'On montre existence et unicité de K_n pour degré ≤ N par récurrence sur N, ces assertions pour N=0 étant triviales'.
'(1) donc ϖ^N = dω^{N−1}' refers to hypothesis (1), the resolution property.
